name: Port scanning & recon - APT29 vs APT41 (+ lab)
description: Blue=APT29, orange=APT41, purple=both, green=technique emulated in Week 9 lab but not in group pages. Source: attack.mitre.org groups G0016, G0096.

techniques.comment: APT29 + APT41. APT29: Conducted widespread scanning of target environments to identify vulnerabilities for exploit | APT41: Used the Acunetix SQL injection scanner and JexBoss (Java apps) in target reconnaissance
APT41. APT29: - | APT41: Brute-forces directories on web servers with various tools/frameworks
APT41. APT29: - | APT41: Uses fofa.su (Shodan-like) for passive scanning of victims
APT41. APT29: - | APT41: APT41 DUST campaign used search engines to research victim servers
APT41. APT29: - | APT41: APT41 DUST campaign accessed external victim websites for target development
APT41. APT29: - | APT41: WIDETONE malware variant used to conduct port scans on specified subnets
APT41. APT29: (listed in campaign data only, no procedure text seen) | APT41: Used MiPing to discover active systems in the victim network
APT41. APT29: - | APT41: Collected MAC addresses; C0017: cmd.exe /c ping %userdomain%
APT41. APT29: - | APT41: Used the net share command as part of network reconnaissance
APT41. APT29: - | APT41: Used netstat; HIGHNOON used to enumerate active RDP sessions
APT29. APT29: SolarWinds: PowerShell Get-ADUser / Get-ADGroupMember | APT41: -
APT29. APT29: Enumerated Azure AD accounts | APT41: -
APT29. APT29: SolarWinds: Get-AcceptedDomain; AdFind to discover federated-domain trusts | APT41: -
APT29. APT29: SolarWinds: AdFind to enumerate domain groups | APT41: -
APT29. APT29: SolarWinds: fsutil to check free disk space | APT41: -
Our lab: port scan of an IP block from outside (same behaviour as Test #1 / scan_python.py). Not listed for APT29/APT41 on the group pages.
